summary: Mission Mars is a 3D browser game that turns a real Martian outpost into a playable mission for students. Players choose one of four real landing sites and a crew role, then run a habitat for six sols (Martian days), balancing power, oxygen, water, food, radiation dose and crew health. Every choice has a cost: heating soil for water drains power, going outside raises radiation dose, and a solar storm forces a decision between shelter and science. Over 25 short mini-games turn each task into hands-on science, and each one ends with a sourced fact. Space weather records from NASA DONKI change what happens in the game, and radiation, gravity, pressure and day length come from real NASA measurements. The game runs in any browser, works offline and supports 8 languages, so any classroom can experience the trade-offs that decide whether a mission succeeds.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mission Mars is a 3D browser game where students live and work on Mars as astronauts. Players choose a real landing site and a crew role, run a Martian base for six days (sols), explore with a rover, and finally fly back to Earth.

HOW IT WORKS

Each day has a real crew routine: eat, exercise, check the base systems, do expedition tasks, send a report to Earth and sleep. Power, water, oxygen, food and radiation must stay in balance, and every choice has a cost. For example, making water uses power, and going outside raises radiation dose. Surprise events like dust storms and solar storms ask players to choose between two strategies and then show the result. More than 25 short mini-games turn each task into hands-on science, and each one ends with a short, sourced fact.

REAL NASA DATA

Solar storm records from NASA DONKI change what happens in the game. Radiation values come from the Curiosity rover's RAD instrument, health and plant facts from NASA OSDR studies, and landing sites and minerals from Mars Trek and MRO CRISM. Every number is labelled as measured, calculated or simplified.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Students learn by making the same kinds of decisions real mission planners make. Teachers only need to share one link. The game works on low-cost devices, needs no installation, works offline and is available in 8 languages.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js (3D graphics), Progressive Web App technology for offline use, esbuild, Python and Playwright for building and testing, and NASA open APIs. We used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI coding and writing assistant.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Players don't just read numbers on a screen. They walk through the base, drive a rover and feel each trade-off in their own day. Data from the real Sun reaches into the game, and the mission ends with a cinematic trip home that explains space travel.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Made for ages 7–12, with a simple mode for young players and a detailed mode for older students. Scientific accuracy, easy controls (keyboard, mouse and touch), classroom use without accounts or installs, and giving players full control over when tasks start.
